summary: CLI-derived nItems and row delimiters feed device arrays; each block handles one row and its 256 threads stride across [rowStart,rowEnd), accumulate val*vec products, reduce within warps and across the block, and one lane stores the row result. Compiled main's counted loop invokes cudaLaunchKernel for every requested trip, increments and compares the iteration counter, then synchronizes before stopping the host timer. The pinned build explicitly targets sm_60 and the available final SASS is the sm_60 kernel; I do not infer compatibility with another architecture. Complete embedded PTX also retains the same work. The sm60 cubin is not native sm86 code; any target-device JIT image is not part of this static evidence. The no-omission conclusion uses the pinned host, source and embedded PTX, with emitted sm60 SASS as additional compiler evidence.
